method: Personally reviewed dated previews, exact prior-match records, availability updates and 10,000-draw simulations. Editorial ratings are not outcome probabilities.
calibration: Uncalibrated research grades. Numeric model frequencies remain separate.

picks.label: Real Madrid ML
picks.reason: Madrid have won six straight in all competitions, while AEK have lost four of their last five. Vinicius is available again in Europe, giving the visitors another attacking option.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Madrid scored four in each of their last two European games; AEK conceded eight across their last two.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: AEK can still threaten through Jovic and Varga at home, while Madrid bring the stronger attack. Keeping the hosts quiet is less certain than the result direction.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Liverpool’s three European games have produced 19 goals. Fenerbahce’s defensive absences offer space, but the hosts can also threaten a visiting defence missing both regular right-back options.

picks.label: Liverpool or Draw
picks.reason: Liverpool have won all three European games; Fenerbahce remain winless in this league phase. Draw cover respects Liverpool’s poor record away to Turkish teams.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: Fenerbahce have drawn both home league-phase games with goals at each end, while Liverpool conceded in all three of theirs.

picks.label: Borussia Dortmund or Draw
picks.reason: Dortmund’s home advantage and Guirassy’s form support draw protection. Betis have won all three European games, so an outright home win carries more risk.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Both attacks have been productive, and Betis can still carry a threat through Isco and Antony despite Hernandez’s absence.

picks.label: Over 8.5 Corners
picks.reason: Both sides have sustained enough attacking pressure in their recent match logs to support a separate corner angle. Recent own-team averages are 7.0 and 5.1 corners.

picks.label: FC Porto or Draw
picks.reason: Porto’s strong domestic run meets a Napoli side with an extensive injury list. The visitors’ away inconsistency makes draw cover the better starting point.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Porto can exploit Napoli’s missing defensive options, while the visitors retain McTominay and a potentially available Hojlund as goal threats.

picks.label: Over 8.5 Corners
picks.reason: The recent corner records provide a separate attacking-volume angle, although this is less secure than the protected result. Recent own-team averages are 5.0 and 4.7 corners.

picks.label: Como or Draw
picks.reason: Como arrive after five straight wins and a 4–1 victory over Manchester United. Lens have lost their last two European games and are missing several attacking and defensive options.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Como scored ten across their first three European games, while Lens have yet to keep a clean sheet in this league phase.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: Lens still carry a home threat through Thauvin and Ivanovic, and Como have conceded on both sides of their win over Manchester United.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Brugge have scored nine across three European games, while PSV come off a seven-goal domestic win. Their attacking form offers a clearer angle than picking a winner.

picks.label: Over 8.5 Corners
picks.reason: The recent corner output from both sides supports continued pressure at both ends. Recent own-team averages are 5.7 and 6.1 corners.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: Brugge arrive on a long winning run with Tresoldi in form, while PSV have Til and Mijnans contributing regularly. Both can trouble the opposing defence.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: The previous six meetings produced 30 goals. Leipzig’s recent European defensive problems meet a City attack with Haaland available and Foden pushing to return.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: Leipzig have enough home attacking threat through Nusa and Romulo, while City’s recent European games have also left openings at the back.

picks.label: Manchester City or Draw
picks.reason: City have won four of the previous six meetings. Draw protection respects Leipzig’s recent recovery and avoids relying on an away clean sheet.

picks.label: Arsenal ML
picks.reason: Arsenal are unbeaten in 18 Champions League games and have won their last two visits here without conceding. Slavia are still seeking their first league-phase win, while Arsenal can call on Saliba again if needed.

picks.label: Under 4.5 Goals
picks.reason: Arsenal’s defensive control and Saka’s absence support a restrained total, with room for a comfortable away win.

picks.label: BTTS No
picks.reason: Arsenal kept 11 clean sheets during their 18-game European unbeaten run, and Slavia have uncertainty around their attacking options. This is a lower-confidence alternative to the result.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Viking’s European games have been open, and Sabah bring a forward line led by Mickels. A goals angle avoids a disputed winner forecast.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: Christiansen and Tripic give Viking a strong home threat, while Sabah have enough pace and recent scoring form to contribute.

picks.label: Viking FK or Draw
picks.reason: Home advantage supports Viking with draw cover, but Sabah’s attacking threat makes the straight home win less attractive.

picks.label: Under 3.5 Goals
picks.reason: Rennes have been tighter at home and Olympiacos can defend in a compact shape. Lepaul is unlikely to play, while El Kaabi remains unavailable for the visitors.

picks.label: Over 8.5 Corners
picks.reason: The last-ten corner logs from both sides support a separate pressure-based market even if finishing remains restrained. Recent own-team averages are 6.4 and 6.5 corners.

picks.label: Stade Rennais or Draw
picks.reason: Rennes are unbeaten at home this season, but Olympiacos are also unbeaten in Europe. Draw protection fits that balance better than an outright home win.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: West Ham are the division’s leading scorers and face a Cardiff defence short of suspended and injured players. Cardiff’s home attack can also contribute to an open game.

picks.label: West Ham United or Draw
picks.reason: West Ham’s attacking quality gives them a route back after consecutive defeats. Draw cover allows for their own defensive uncertainty.

picks.label: BTTS Yes
picks.reason: Cardiff’s defensive problems support a visiting goal, but West Ham have also been conceding often enough to leave the hosts a route in.

picks.label: Middlesbrough or Draw
picks.reason: Middlesbrough have one league defeat all season and four wins in their last five. Wrexham have lost their last two without scoring, so the leaders with draw cover are the stronger result angle.

picks.label: Over 2.5 Goals
picks.reason: Boro have scored 30 in 13 league games, though Wrexham’s recent scoreless run limits confidence in a high total.

picks.label: Over 8.5 Corners
picks.reason: Boro’s attacking volume and the recent corner records support another route without asking Wrexham to score. Recent own-team averages are 4.5 and 6.7 corners.

picks.label: Under 3.5 Goals
picks.reason: Bristol City and Wolves have the quieter recent scoring profile on this slate. Wolves may also be without Jordan James, while the home side are deciding how much to change in attack.

picks.label: Wolverhampton Wanderers or Draw
picks.reason: Wolves bring the stronger league position, but Bristol City’s home resistance makes draw cover preferable to a straight away win.

picks.label: Over 8.5 Corners
picks.reason: Both teams’ recent corner output supports pressure around the boxes without requiring a high-scoring game. Recent own-team averages are 6.2 and 6.7 corners.
